277	    this[kStrictContentLength] = strictContentLength == null ? true : strictContentLength

281	    this[kHTTPContext] = null

284	    // HTTP/2 window sizes are set to higher defaults than Node.js core for better performance:
285	    // - initialWindowSize: 262144 (256KB) vs Node.js default 65535 (64KB - 1)
286	    //   Allows more data to be sent before requiring acknowledgment, improving throughput
287	    //   especially on high-latency networks. This matches common production HTTP/2 servers.
288	    // - connectionWindowSize: 524288 (512KB) vs Node.js default (none set)
289	    //   Provides better flow control for the entire connection across multiple streams.
290	    this[kHTTP2InitialWindowSize] = initialWindowSize != null ? initialWindowSize : 262144
291	    this[kHTTP2ConnectionWindowSize] = connectionWindowSize != null ? connectionWindowSize : 524288
292	    this[kPingInterval] = pingInterval != null ? pingInterval : 60e3 // Default ping interval for h2 - 1 minute

294	    // kQueue is built up of 3 sections separated by
295	    // the kRunningIdx and kPendingIdx indices.
296	    // |   complete   |   running   |   pending   |
297	    //                ^ kRunningIdx ^ kPendingIdx ^ kQueue.length
298	    // kRunningIdx points to the first running element.
299	    // kPendingIdx points to the first pending element.
300	    // This implements a fast queue with an amortized
301	    // time of O(1).
302	
303	    this[kQueue] = []
304	    this[kRunningIdx] = 0
305	    this[kPendingIdx] = 0
306	
307	    this[kResume] = (sync) => resume(this, sync)
308	    this[kOnError] = (err) => onError(this, err)
309	  }
310	
311	  get pipelining () {
312	    return this[kPipelining]
313	  }
314	
315	  set pipelining (value) {
316	    this[kPipelining] = value
317	    this[kResume](true)
318	  }
319	
320	  get stats () {
321	    return new ClientStats(this)
322	  }
323	
324	  get [kPending] () {
325	    return this[kQueue].length - this[kPendingIdx]
326	  }
327	
328	  get [kRunning] () {
329	    return this[kPendingIdx] - this[kRunningIdx]
330	  }
331	
332	  get [kSize] () {
333	    return this[kQueue].length - this[kRunningIdx]
334	  }
335	
336	  get [kConnected] () {
337	    return !!this[kHTTPContext] && !this[kConnecting] && !this[kHTTPContext].destroyed
338	  }
339	
340	  get [kBusy] () {
341	    // The `kPending > 0` check below is the gate Pool uses to decide whether
342	    // to spin up an additional Client. For h1 that fan-out is correct —
343	    // each socket only handles one pipelined request at a time. Once an h2
344	    // context is attached we want concurrent dispatches to multiplex onto
345	    // the shared session, so suppress that signal in the h2 case.
346	    const allowsMux = this[kHTTPContext]?.version === 'h2'
347	
348	    return Boolean(
349	      this[kHTTPContext]?.busy(null) ||
350	      (this[kSize] >= (getMaxConcurrent(this) || 1)) ||
351	      (this[kPending] > 0 && !allowsMux)
352	    )
353	  }
354	
355	  [kConnect] (cb) {
356	    connect(this)
357	    this.once('connect', cb)
358	  }
359	
360	  [kDispatch] (opts, handler) {
361	    const request = new Request(this[kUrl].origin, opts, handler)
362	
363	    this[kQueue].push(request)
364	    if (this[kResuming]) {
365	      // Do nothing.
366	    } else if (util.bodyLength(request.body) == null && util.isIterable(request.body)) {
367	      // Wait a tick in case stream/iterator is ended in the same tick.
368	      this[kResuming] = 1
369	      queueMicrotask(() => resume(this))
370	    } else {
371	      this[kResume](true)
372	    }
373	
374	    if (this[kResuming] && this[kNeedDrain] !== 2 && this[kBusy]) {
375	      this[kNeedDrain] = 2
376	    }
377	
378	    return this[kNeedDrain] < 2
379	  }

381	  [kClose] () {
382	    // TODO: for H2 we need to gracefully flush the remaining enqueued
383	    // request and close each stream.
384	    return new Promise((resolve) => {
385	      if (this[kSize]) {
386	        this[kClosedResolve] = resolve
387	      } else {
388	        resolve(null)
389	      }
390	    })
391	  }
392	
393	  [kDestroy] (err) {
394	    return new Promise((resolve) => {
395	      const requests = this[kQueue].splice(this[kPendingIdx])
396	      for (let i = 0; i < requests.length; i++) {
397	        const request = requests[i]
398	        if (request != null) {
399	          util.errorRequest(this, request, err)
400	        }
401	      }
402	
403	      const callback = () => {
404	        if (this[kClosedResolve]) {
405	          // TODO (fix): Should we error here with ClientDestroyedError?
406	          this[kClosedResolve]()
407	          this[kClosedResolve] = null
408	        }
409	        resolve(null)
410	      }
411	
412	      if (this[kHTTPContext]) {
413	        this[kHTTPContext].destroy(err, callback)
414	        this[kHTTPContext] = null
415	      } else {
416	        queueMicrotask(callback)
417	      }
418	
419	      this[kResume]()
420	    })
421	  }
422	}
423	
424	function onError (client, err) {
425	  if (
426	    client[kRunning] === 0 &&
427	    err.code !== 'UND_ERR_INFO' &&
428	    err.code !== 'UND_ERR_SOCKET'
429	  ) {
430	    // Error is not caused by running request and not a recoverable
431	    // socket error.
432	
433	    assert(client[kPendingIdx] === client[kRunningIdx])
434	
435	    const requests = client[kQueue].splice(client[kRunningIdx])
436	
437	    for (let i = 0; i < requests.length; i++) {
438	      const request = requests[i]
439	      if (request != null) {
440	        util.errorRequest(client, request, err)
441	      }
442	    }
443	    assert(client[kSize] === 0)
444	  }
445	}

447	/**
448	 * @param {Client} client
449	 * @returns {void}
450	 */
451	function connect (client) {
452	  assert(!client[kConnecting])
453	  assert(!client[kHTTPContext])
454	
455	  let { host, hostname, protocol, port } = client[kUrl]
456	
457	  // Resolve ipv6
458	  if (hostname[0] === '[') {
459	    const idx = hostname.indexOf(']')
460	
461	    assert(idx !== -1)
462	    const ip = hostname.substring(1, idx)
463	
464	    assert(net.isIPv6(ip))
465	    hostname = ip
466	  }
467	
468	  client[kConnecting] = true
469	
470	  if (channels.beforeConnect.hasSubscribers) {
471	    channels.beforeConnect.publish({
472	      connectParams: {
473	        host,
474	        hostname,
475	        protocol,
476	        port,
477	        version: client[kHTTPContext]?.version,
478	        servername: client[kServerName],
479	        localAddress: client[kLocalAddress]
480	      },
481	      connector: client[kConnector]
482	    })
483	  }
484	
485	  try {
486	    client[kConnector]({
487	      host,
488	      hostname,
489	      protocol,
490	      port,
491	      servername: client[kServerName],
492	      localAddress: client[kLocalAddress]
493	    }, (err, socket) => {
494	      if (err) {
495	        handleConnectError(client, err, { host, hostname, protocol, port })
496	        client[kResume]()
497	        return
498	      }
499	
500	      if (client.destroyed) {
501	        util.destroy(socket.on('error', noop), new ClientDestroyedError())
502	        client[kResume]()
503	        return
504	      }
505	
506	      assert(socket)
507	
508	      try {
509	        client[kHTTPContext] = socket.alpnProtocol === 'h2'
510	          ? connectH2(client, socket)
511	          : connectH1(client, socket)
512	      } catch (err) {
513	        socket.destroy().on('error', noop)
514	        handleConnectError(client, err, { host, hostname, protocol, port })
515	        client[kResume]()
516	        return
517	      }
518	
519	      client[kConnecting] = false
520	
521	      socket[kCounter] = 0
522	      socket[kMaxRequests] = client[kMaxRequests]
523	      socket[kClient] = client
524	      socket[kError] = null
525	
526	      if (channels.connected.hasSubscribers) {
527	        channels.connected.publish({
528	          connectParams: {
529	            host,
530	            hostname,
531	            protocol,
532	            port,
533	            version: client[kHTTPContext]?.version,
534	            servername: client[kServerName],
535	            localAddress: client[kLocalAddress]
536	          },
537	          connector: client[kConnector],
538	          socket
539	        })
540	      }
541	
542	      client.emit('connect', client[kUrl], [client])
543	      client[kResume]()
544	    })
545	  } catch (err) {
546	    handleConnectError(client, err, { host, hostname, protocol, port })
547	    client[kResume]()
548	  }
549	}
550	
551	function handleConnectError (client, err, { host, hostname, protocol, port }) {
552	  if (client.destroyed) {
553	    return
554	  }
555	
556	  client[kConnecting] = false
557	
558	  if (channels.connectError.hasSubscribers) {
559	    channels.connectError.publish({
560	      connectParams: {
561	        host,
562	        hostname,
563	        protocol,
564	        port,
565	        version: client[kHTTPContext]?.version,
566	        servername: client[kServerName],
567	        localAddress: client[kLocalAddress]
568	      },
569	      connector: client[kConnector],
570	      error: err
571	    })
572	  }
573	
574	  if (err.code === 'ERR_TLS_CERT_ALTNAME_INVALID') {
575	    const running = client[kQueue].splice(client[kRunningIdx], client[kRunning])
576	    client[kPendingIdx] = client[kRunningIdx]
577	
578	    for (let i = 0; i < running.length; i++) {
579	      util.errorRequest(client, running[i], err)
580	    }
581	
582	    while (client[kPending] > 0 && client[kQueue][client[kPendingIdx]].servername === client[kServerName]) {
583	      const request = client[kQueue].splice(client[kPendingIdx], 1)[0]
584	      util.errorRequest(client, request, err)
585	    }
586	  } else {
587	    onError(client, err)
588	  }
589	
590	  client.emit('connectionError', client[kUrl], [client], err)
591	}
592	
593	function emitDrain (client) {
594	  client[kNeedDrain] = 0
595	  client.emit('drain', client[kUrl], [client])
596	}
597	
598	function resume (client, sync) {
599	  if (client[kResuming] === 2) {
600	    return
601	  }
602	
603	  client[kResuming] = 2
604	
605	  _resume(client, sync)
606	  client[kResuming] = 0
607	
608	  if (client[kRunningIdx] > 256) {
609	    client[kQueue].splice(0, client[kRunningIdx])
610	    client[kPendingIdx] -= client[kRunningIdx]
611	    client[kRunningIdx] = 0
612	  }
613	}
614	
615	function _resume (client, sync) {
616	  while (true) {
617	    if (client.destroyed) {
618	      assert(client[kPending] === 0)
619	      return
620	    }
621	
622	    if (client[kClosedResolve] && !client[kSize]) {
623	      client[kClosedResolve]()
624	      client[kClosedResolve] = null
625	      return
626	    }
627	
628	    if (client[kHTTPContext]) {
629	      client[kHTTPContext].resume()
630	    }
631	
632	    if (client[kBusy]) {
633	      client[kNeedDrain] = 2
634	    } else if (client[kNeedDrain] === 2) {
635	      if (sync) {
636	        client[kNeedDrain] = 1
637	        queueMicrotask(() => emitDrain(client))
638	      } else {
639	        emitDrain(client)
640	      }
641	      continue
642	    }
643	
644	    if (client[kPending] === 0) {
645	      return
646	    }
647	
648	    if (client[kRunning] >= (getMaxConcurrent(client) || 1)) {
649	      return
650	    }
651	
652	    const request = client[kQueue][client[kPendingIdx]]
653	
654	    if (request === null) {
655	      return
656	    }
657	
658	    if (client[kUrl].protocol === 'https:' && client[kServerName] !== request.servername) {
659	      if (client[kRunning] > 0) {
660	        return
661	      }
662	
663	      client[kServerName] = request.servername
664	      client[kHTTPContext]?.destroy(new InformationalError('servername changed'), () => {
665	        client[kHTTPContext] = null
666	        resume(client)
667	      })
668	    }
669	
670	    if (client[kConnecting]) {
671	      return
672	    }

# Errors

Undici exposes a variety of error objects that you can use to enhance your error handling.
You can find all the error objects inside the `errors` key.

```js
import { errors } from 'undici'
```

| Error                                | Error Codes                           | Description                                                               |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `UndiciError`                        | `UND_ERR`                             | all errors below are extended from `UndiciError`.                         |
| `ConnectTimeoutError`                | `UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`             | socket is destroyed due to connect timeout.                               |
| `HeadersTimeoutError`                | `UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT`             | socket is destroyed due to headers timeout.                               |

  remoteAddress?: string
  remotePort?: number
  remoteFamily?: string
  timeout?: number
  bytesWritten?: number
  bytesRead?: number

Fixed the infinite loop. Here's what was happening and what changed.

**Root cause of the loop:** `ProxyAgent`'s tunnel connector (`lib/dispatcher/proxy-agent.js:230`) passed the raw failure of the `CONNECT` handshake to `callback`. That lands in `client.js` → `handleConnectError` → `onError`, which deliberately treats `UND_ERR_SOCKET` (and `UND_ERR_INFO`) as *recoverable* — so queued requests are left in the queue, `resume()` runs, `connect()` fires again, and the client hammers the proxy forever. The existing `SecureProxyConnectionError` wrap right above it exists for exactly this reason (its comment says "avoid loop in client.js#connect"), just for the TLS-altname case only.

**Change** — `lib/dispatcher/proxy-agent.js:230`: socket-level failures of the tunnel handshake are now wrapped in a new non-retryable `ProxyConnectionError` (`UND_ERR_PRX_CONN`, original error kept as `.cause`), so the request fails immediately after one attempt. Supporting edits: the error class in `lib/core/errors.js`, `types/errors.d.ts` + `test/types/errors.test-d.ts`, a row in `docs/docs/api/Errors.md`, and a regression test in `test/proxy-agent.js` asserting the error and that the proxy sees exactly one connection.

Verified with your reproduction: before, ~2144 proxy connections in 2s and no result; after, `errored: UND_ERR_PRX_CONN Proxy connection failed: other side closed connections = 1`. `test/proxy-agent.js` (37 tests), `test/socks5-proxy-agent.js`, `test/env-http-proxy-agent.js`, `test/client-errors.js`, `test/proxy.js`, `test/retry-handler-controller-proxy.js` all pass. I couldn't run `npm run lint` — the sandbox declined that command — so style is matched by hand against the surrounding code.

**On your first question (why the connection closes):** that part isn't an undici bug. `ProxyAgent` defaults to `proxyTunnel: true`, so it sends `CONNECT example.com:80` to your proxy. A `node:http` server with no `'connect'` listener destroys the socket on a CONNECT request — hence `SocketError: other side closed`. Your `Client` example works because it sends an ordinary absolute-URI request, which your handler does implement. To get that behavior from `ProxyAgent`, construct it with `proxyTunnel: false` (for an `http:` proxy and `http:` target this uses the non-tunneling `Http1ProxyWrapper` path), or add a `'connect'` handler to your proxy server. I left the tunneling default alone — silently falling back to a plaintext forwarded request when CONNECT fails would downgrade the proxying contract.
